title: OR-Agent: Bridging Evolutionary Search and Structured Research for Automated Algorithm Discovery

mechanism.domainTask: Multi-agent algorithm discovery for combinatorial optimization and cooperative-driving simulation
mechanism.populationDetail: A shared cross-round solution database coexists with explicit per-Lead-Agent research trees whose nodes retain hypotheses, implementations, and evidence.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The persistent database stores evaluated solutions and can return current elites, but archive admission, pruning, and whether it is a separate bounded elite set are unspecified.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Database persistence/insertion is combined with local tree expansion that retains only children improving on their parent; database maintenance details are omitted.
mechanism.generationDetail: LLM-driven idea variation and crossover-like recombination create tree children, followed by iterative localized code/parameter refinement within each candidate's experiment loop.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Evaluators provide metrics, logs, errors, and traces; callbacks can expose additional simulation state. Both structured outcomes and generated summaries are reused by Experiment, Lead, and Idea Agents.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: One or more parent solutions are retrieved from the shared solution database. The paper describes stochastic sampling versus elite-biased selection with temperature interpolation but not exact probabilities or cardinality; best-leaf selection chooses an expansion node, not another solution parent.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A research-agent workflow combines shared persistent memory, tree-structured hypothesis expansion, coordinated sibling idea generation, iterative environment instrumentation, and hierarchical reflection; current fields do not fully capture this cross-level architecture.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/OR-Agent Bridging Evolutionary Search and Structured Research for Automated Algorithm Discovery.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Existing survey coverage is limited to the tree, coordinator role, and application table. Consider missing feedback, evaluation, model, exploration-control, and parent-selection placements. Do not infer fixed parent count, archive admission, exact prompt template, or a complete operator-selection policy. Parallel evaluation is medium confidence.
